title: Datacube statistics summary
description: The measured answer a time-series datacube reduces to: one record per pass, the net baseline-to-latest change, and (with a blocks grid) which part of the site moved and between which two passes. Emitted identically by `umbra_py.stack_stats`, `umbra stack --stats --json` (under the manifest's `stats` key), `POST /artifacts/stats` on `umbra serve`, and the `stack_stats` agent tool (MCP / LangChain / LlamaIndex).

count.description: How many passes the cube holds (the length of `passes`).

units.description: The cube's own pixel units, which the per-pass distribution is reported in. Change is always reported in decibels regardless.

product_type.description: The asset the cube was built from, or null when the cube records none.

change_threshold_db.description: How many decibels a cell had to move between two passes to count as changed.

provenance.description: What the cube's sources say their pixel values are, read off their `UMBRA_*` conversion tags. Present only when the sources recorded one, so its absence means "the published products as delivered" rather than "unknown". It is also what decides whether the first caveat calls these decibels relative or calibrated.

quantile_method.description: Present only under `windowed=True`, where the per-pass percentiles are histogram estimates rather than exact. Its absence means every number in the summary is exact.

quantile_bin_db.description: The histogram bin width those estimates are good to, in decibels. Present exactly when `quantile_method` is.

grid.description: The shared grid every pass was co-registered onto.

cell_size.description: `[x, y]` cell size in the grid's own units (degrees for a geographic CRS, metres for a projected one).

cell_area_m2.description: Ground area of one cell, or null on a geographic grid whose cells are not equal-area (which is also why `changed_area_km2` is null there).

bounds.description: `[minx, miny, maxx, maxy]` in the grid's CRS.

extent.description: Whether the grid is the acquisitions' shared footprint or their union.

detection.description: Present only on a multi-pass cube whose looks could be read. Its absence means there was no comparison to weigh (a single pass), or that nothing measured the looks -- never that speckle is not a factor.

passes.description: One record per acquisition, oldest first.

net_change.description: The first pass compared to the last. Null for a single-pass cube, and for a series whose first and last passes share no valid cell.

spatial.description: Present only when a blocks grid was asked for (`stack_stats(blocks=N)` / `umbra stack --blocks N`).

attribution.description: The attribution CC BY 4.0 requires, which must survive into anything quoting these numbers.

caveats.description: What these numbers do and do not mean, derived from the cube itself rather than fixed: the calibration, the flattening, a subtracted noise floor and how it was obtained, a speckle filter and what it cost, the speckle detection floor `detection` reports (and, when the observed change does not clear it, that it did not), a geographic grid that cannot report area, and windowed percentiles.

provenanceRecord.description: A raster's `UMBRA_*` conversion record, keys lowercased and de-prefixed. See `stack-provenance.schema.json` for the report that groups a selection by it.

detection.description: What speckle alone does to a change measured at `change_threshold_db`. Speckle is not an error bar on a mean: it is the dominant variation in a single cell, and at one look the pass-to-pass decibel difference of *unchanged* ground has a 7.9 dB spread. So a `changed_fraction` is evidence only to the degree it stands clear of this floor.

looks.description: The equivalent number of looks the floor was computed at: the median of the passes that gave a reading, clamped to at least one look (no product has fewer). Every pass keeps its own `looks`, so a series whose passes disagree is visible rather than averaged away.

cell_sigma_db.description: The standard deviation, in decibels, of the pass-to-pass difference of a single *unchanged* cell at `looks`. Exactly `(10/ln 10) * sqrt(2 * trigamma(looks))`, since an L-look intensity is a gamma variate whose natural log has variance `trigamma(L)`.

false_alarm_fraction.description: The share of *unchanged* cells speckle alone pushes past `change_threshold_db`. Exact rather than approximate -- `2 * I_(1/(1+f))(looks, looks)` with `f = 10**(change_threshold_db/10)`, the regularized incomplete beta -- because a normal approximation is wrong by tens of per cent near one look, which is where the answer matters most. Read it against `net_change.changed_fraction`: the observed share is only evidence to the extent it exceeds this one. Because the looks read low on a textured scene, this is an upper bound on the false alarms rather than a flattering estimate.

target_threshold_db.description: The threshold that would hold speckle's false alarms to `false_alarm_target` at these looks. A `change_threshold_db` below it is counting interference; speckle-filtering the cube (`to_stack(speckle_filter=...)`) raises the looks and brings this number down.

change.description: A signed decibel comparison between two passes over the cells both observed.

compared_cells.description: Cells valid in both passes. A pair sharing none has no record at all (null) rather than a record of zero.

mean_delta_db.description: Mean signed change, positive where the later pass is brighter.

mean_abs_delta_db.description: Mean unsigned change: how much ground moved, whichever way.

brightened_fraction.description: Fraction of compared cells that rose by at least `change_threshold_db`.

dimmed_fraction.description: Fraction that fell by at least `change_threshold_db`.

changed_area_km2.description: The changed cells as ground area, or null on a geographic grid, where counting cells measures nothing.

pass.description: One acquisition's distribution on the shared grid, plus its change against the pass before it.

mean.description: In the cube's own `units`. Null when the pass has no valid cell on the shared grid, as are the four statistics below.

looks.description: This pass's equivalent number of looks, read off the cube's own 16-cell blocks as the median block's `mean**2 / variance` of detected power. It describes the cells the numbers beside it are quoted about rather than the source product: `to_stack` decimates onto a shared grid, and decimation averages speckle down. Scene structure inflates a block's variance and so deflates the ratio, which means this reads low -- it is a floor on the looks present, not a claim about them. Null where no block could be read: a cube smaller than one block, or a pass whose blocks were nodata.

change_vs_previous.description: Against the pass before it. Null for the first pass.

interval.description: One consecutive pass-to-pass step of a block, named by both ends.

spatial.description: The site cut into a coarse grid, so a change has a place as well as a size — and, when the cube carried a speckle `detection` floor, whether each block's change stands clear of it.

bounds_crs.description: The CRS each block's `bounds` is in — the cube's own grid.

peak_block.description: The block that moved most overall, or null when no block had two comparable passes.

grid_text.description: The net signed change per block as a north-up ASCII heat-grid, one line per row.

blocks.description: Every block, row-major from the northwest.

center_lonlat.description: `[lon, lat]` to map or geocode the block by, or null when the grid's CRS could not be transformed to lon/lat.

net_change.description: First pass to last, over this block. Null where the block has no cell both passes observed.

peak_interval.description: The consecutive pair of passes this block moved most between — its "when" answer. Null where no step could be measured.

detection.description: How this block's net change weighs against the cube's speckle floor. Present only when the cube carried a `detection` floor and this block had two comparable passes; absent otherwise.

series.description: Every consecutive step, oldest first, that `peak_interval` was picked from. Present only under `block_series=True`, which is what tells a steady drift apart from a single step.

stands_clear.description: Whether the headline block's net `changed_fraction` stands clear of the cube's speckle floor by the same margin the cube-level advisory uses. Present only when the cube carried a `detection` floor. `false` says the biggest mover is still inside the floor — interference rather than change.

blockDetection.description: One block's net change weighed against the cube's speckle detection floor. The floor is a per-cell expectation (`detection.false_alarm_fraction`) and so is exact for a block of any size, but a block is measured over far fewer cells than the whole scene, so its observed `changed_fraction` scatters more widely around it — read `stands_clear` together with `compared_cells` rather than on its own.

false_alarm_fraction.description: The cube-wide per-cell floor `detection.false_alarm_fraction`, repeated here so a block record can be weighed on its own. Read it against this block's `net_change.changed_fraction`.

compared_cells.description: The number of cells both compared passes observed in this block — the sample size behind its `changed_fraction`, and how far to trust `stands_clear`. Equal to `net_change.compared_cells`.

stands_clear.description: Whether this block's `net_change.changed_fraction` exceeds the floor by the same `DETECTION_EXCESS_WARN` margin the cube-level advisory uses. `false` means the block's change does not stand clear of what speckle produces here.
